correctness.rationale: Verified from the actual RESULT.md and all seven source Git entries: for q=n-1, the regular solution h_s(x)=2F1(a_s,q-a_s;1;x), a_s(q-a_s)=s/c, yields E exp(-sT_b)=1/h_s(b). Product factorization gives m=ΣA_k b^k/c and Var=m^2-2ΣA_k b^k S_k/c^2. Thus D=2 E_w S_K/c with S_k strictly increasing from 0 to H_q/q; differentiation gives dD/d log(b)=2 Cov_w(K,S_K)/c>0. Since A_k∼k^(q-2)/q!, the normalizing weights diverge at b↑1 (log for q=1), escape finite k, and D↑2H_q/(cq). Independently the mean ODE gives m_2=-log(1-b)/c and m_n∼(1-b)^-(q-1)/(cq(q-1)) for q>=2, hence exactly the claimed relative-variance rates. Nondegenerate stopped diffusion has Var>0; boundary conventions b<1, x=0 entrance, c>0 and fixed n were checked. Independently coded high-precision positive-series evaluation and an ODE quadrature at q=1,2,3,6 and b=.05,.25,.7,.93 (16 cases), with strict inequalities and mean agreement; finite checks supplement the universal proof. The complete seven-entry Git tree SHA was independently reconstructed and matched 0e2f66...; no VERIFY_OK was used as proof.

value.rationale: The underlying Fubini--Study Brownian state-preparation problem and target-fidelity passage are natural and physically motivated. The mean-weighted deficit m(1-CV^2) isolates the first additive-time deviation from the exponential rare-target clock. Its strict ordering over every threshold and sharp dimension-dependent harmonic ceiling is a genuine structural comparison of fluctuation statistics beyond fixed-threshold Jacobi moment evaluation; the logarithmic versus power-law approach creates a natural dimension-two boundary. Its value does not require a new generic Jacobi transform, a paper-sized result, or downstream physical validation. The fact is not a mere parameter substitution or an arbitrary unmotivated finite slice.

final_claim: As stated: for integer n>=2, c>0 and b in (0,1), the mean-weighted squared-CV deficit of the projective-fidelity Jacobi first-passage time started from zero is strictly increasing, positive and strictly below 2H_(n-1)/(c(n-1)); it converges to that sharp ceiling as b approaches 1, giving the asserted logarithmic (n=2) and epsilon^(n-2) (n>=3) correction to squared CV=1.
limitations: Only the canonical isotropic Brownian generator from F_0=0; no finite-step random walk or microscopic quantum dynamics.
The proof establishes two moments and the sharp deficit, not distributional convergence of the full rescaled T_b law.
Independent bounded high-precision computations verify finite sample choices only, not infinite domains.
Best-of-knowledge priority with generic Jacobi and same-model transform coverage explicitly credited; no publication certification.
